opportunities.problem_summary: A real LiteLLM operator reports that x-litellm-timeout=10 is not an end-to-end bound when a router retries after upstream 503/429 Retry-After sleeps. The independently authored open PR #50013 makes the sleep respect the remaining monotonic deadline, but the inspected retry branch can call the provider again after a capped sleep has consumed that same deadline; per-attempt timeout is not visibly reduced to the remaining deadline in the changed code.

source_checked_failure_boundary.sequence: When one upstream failure occurs near the client's deadline, the patch performs await sleep(min(retry_after, remaining)) and then enters make_call without another time.monotonic check. A 0.1-second remaining budget with Retry-After 6 can be entirely consumed by that sleep, yet a new provider attempt is still started. That attempt still sees the original per-attempt timeout instead of a demonstrated remaining-budget cap. Related fallback and streamed retry routes require separate current-source review.
source_checked_failure_boundary.nonfit_control: If an attempt begins with positive remaining time and finishes within that time, successful response remains permitted; an unspecified caller deadline must preserve the pre-existing retry policy. A purely mocked sleep argument assertion does not prove the later provider attempt was prevented.
source_checked_failure_boundary.body_timeout_header_distinction: The user issue explicitly includes body timeout. At PR HEAD a5c3391, LiteLLMProxyRequestSetup.add_litellm_data_for_backend_llm_call receives request_data, but stamps data['request_deadline'] only under `if header_timeout is not None`; `request_data.get('timeout')` is recognized separately for a client_side_timeout marker. The router retry path reads only `request_deadline`, so for a body-only `timeout` it visibly has no new end-to-end bound from this constructor. Check downstream propagation before asserting a runtime bypass.

useful_contributions: In the independent implementer's current PR/branch, inject a deterministic monotonic clock and a provider-call counter: after a retry is capped to the last 0.1 second of a 10-second budget, assert no further make_call is started once the deadline is exhausted. The current PR tests the sleep bound but does not establish this post-sleep assertion.

Assert the timeout actually passed to every provider attempt is bounded by the smaller of configured per-attempt timeout and the remaining caller deadline; use a controlled slow mock provider as a negative, and an in-budget fast provider as positive. Do not treat a source-only prediction as an executed production failure.

Add the separately requested BODY-only case: send `{'timeout': 10}` without x-litellm-timeout or x-stainless-timeout, simulate fast upstream 503 with Retry-After 6 and two or more retries, and assert a true 10-second request-wide budget. Compare the equivalent header case and unchanged no-timeout control. This is not merely a header parser test; source currently derives a monotonic deadline only from headers.

Check initial call, later retry, fallback chain and streaming-first-byte boundary separately against the exact present code. Fix only the missing boundaries consistent with current maintainers' chosen semantics and existing code ownership.

Before any contribution re-read the current PR HEAD and existing review decisions. If already fixed, report a non-fit and do not repeat a known finding. Return a concise source/test link only if a different participant independently performs the work.
